title: The structural basis for LRRK2's activation and autoinhibition.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the PDB IDs out of the full text. About 20 are cited; 9Y67, 9Y68, 9Y7A, 9YBL and others appear new. Fetched the RCSB (Protein Data Bank) metadata for 9Y67: it is public and cites this paper. A HEAD request on its mmCIF (structure file) download returned 200. I did not parse the coordinates. The Europe PMC supplement listing timed out, so I never opened Table S1 (the accession table).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the deposits are cryo-EM (cryo-electron microscopy) maps and models of LRRK2 (leucine-rich repeat kinase 2) in its GTP- and GDP-bound states (two nucleotides that switch it on or off), plus the G2019S and R1441C mutants. Cell-based kinase assays are described only as figures.

a1_downloadable.note: PDB entry 9Y67 is public on RCSB and its file download returns 200 (checked). The other entries and EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) maps were not checked one by one.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The deposits are 3D structures of one protein, not a table of measured outcomes. Any label, such as 'active vs autoinhibited state', would have to be built by hand from the structures.

a3_inputs_present.note: Coordinates and sequence are inside the mmCIF files.

a4_units_stated.note: There is no tabular measurement with units. Kinase-activity numbers exist only in figures (paper text).

a5_enough_rows.note: Roughly 15–20 structures of a single protein, found by counting PDB IDs in the text. That is far below the ~400 minimum, even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 GB of models (maps would be larger)

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked against Table S1, which I could not retrieve.

a8_label_provenance.note: Structures come from experiments, but no label column exists to trace.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: the data are about 20 structures of one protein, with no table of measured labels.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's 3D shape to predict whether it is switched on (active) or switched off (autoinhibited).
plain_idea.train_on: Cryo-EM structures of the LRRK2 protein in different nucleotide-bound and mutant states. There are about 20, all of one protein (counted from PDB IDs in the text).
plain_idea.predict: An active or inactive state for each structure, assigned by hand by the authors from structural features. It is not a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Researchers developing Parkinson's drugs that target LRRK2 care about its active and inactive states, but 20 structures of one protein are a case study, not a training set.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed because Part A failed.

ml_idea: None that the data supports. The structures could serve at most as a few held-out test cases for predicting protein conformational states.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited structures in Table S1 (about 20 from the text). Too few to train on.

verdict_reason: This is a structural biology paper: about 20 cryo-EM structures of a single protein (LRRK2). There is no label column and nowhere near enough examples to train a model, so A2 and A5 fail.
